passages.text: After this, the Moabites and Ammonites, together with some of the Meunites, came to make war against Jehoshaphat.
passages.sermon:
The Moabites were a people who lived near Israel.
The Ammonites were another people who lived near Israel.
The Meunites were a group who joined with them.
Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah.
After these things happened, the Moabites came.
The Ammonites also came.
The Meunites came with them.
They all came to fight against Jehoshaphat.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י אַֽחֲרֵיכֵ֡ן בָּ֣אוּ בְנֵי־ מוֹאָב֩ וּבְנֵ֨י עַמּ֜וֹן וְעִמָּהֶ֧ם׀ מֵֽהָעַמּוֹנִ֛ים עַל־ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט לַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

passages.text: Then some men came and told Jehoshaphat, “A vast army is coming against you from Edom, from beyond the Sea; they are already in Hazazon-tamar” (that is, En-gedi).
passages.sermon:
Some men came to Jehoshaphat.
They spoke to Jehoshaphat.
They said, “A vast army is coming against you.
This army comes from Edom.
They come from beyond the Sea.
They are already in Hazazon-tamar.
Hazazon-tamar is also called En-gedi.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ וַיַּגִּ֤ידוּ לִֽיהוֹשָׁפָט֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בָּ֣א עָלֶ֜יךָ הָמ֥וֹן רָ֛ב מֵעֵ֥בֶר לַיָּ֖ם מֵאֲרָ֑ם וְהִנָּם֙ בְּחַֽצְצ֣וֹן תָּמָ֔ר הִ֖יא עֵ֥ין גֶּֽדִי׃

passages.text: Jehoshaphat was alarmed and set his face to seek the LORD. And he proclaimed a fast throughout Judah.
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah.
He heard that a vast army was coming against him.
Jehoshaphat became afraid.
He decided to seek the LORD.
Jehoshaphat turned his attention to God.
He called for a fast in all Judah.
He told everyone in Judah to stop eating and pray.
passages.original: וַיִּרָ֕א וַיִּתֵּ֧ן יְהוֹשָׁפָ֛ט אֶת־ פָּנָ֖יו לִדְר֣וֹשׁ לַיהוָ֑ה וַיִּקְרָא־ צ֖וֹם עַל־ כָּל־ יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: So the people of Judah gathered to seek the LORD, and indeed, they came from all the cities of Judah to seek Him.
passages.sermon:
The people of Judah gathered together.
They wanted to seek the LORD.
People came from every city in Judah.
They all came to seek the LORD.
passages.original: וַיִּקָּבְצ֣וּ יְהוּדָ֔ה לְבַקֵּ֖שׁ מֵֽיְהוָ֑ה גַּ֚ם מִכָּל־ עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה בָּ֖אוּ לְבַקֵּ֥שׁ אֶת־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Then Jehoshaphat stood in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem in the house of the LORD in front of the new courtyard and said, “O LORD, God of our fathers, are You not the God who is in heaven, and do You not rule over all the kingdoms of the nations? Power and might are in Your hand, and no one can stand against You.
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah.
He stood in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem.
He stood in the house of the LORD.
He stood in front of the new courtyard.
Jehoshaphat spoke to God.
He said, “LORD, You are the God of our fathers.
You are the God in heaven.
You rule over all the kingdoms of the nations.
Power is in Your hand.
Might is in Your hand.
No one can stand against You.”
passages.original: וַיַּעֲמֹ֣ד יְהוֹשָׁפָ֗ט בִּקְהַ֧ל יְהוּדָ֛ה וִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה לִפְנֵ֖י הֶחָצֵ֥ר הַחֲדָשָֽׁה׃ וַיֹּאמַ֗ר יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י אֲבֹתֵ֙ינוּ֙ הֲלֹ֨א אַתָּֽה־ ה֤וּא אֱלֹהִים֙ בַּשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְאַתָּ֣ה מוֹשֵׁ֔ל בְּכֹ֖ל מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וּבְיָדְךָ֙ כֹּ֣חַ וּגְבוּרָ֔ה וְאֵ֥ין עִמְּךָ֖ לְהִתְיַצֵּֽב׃

passages.text: Our God, did You not drive out the inhabitants of this land before Your people Israel and give it forever to the descendants of Abraham Your friend?
passages.sermon:
God is the God of Israel.
God drove out the people who lived in this land.
God did this before His people Israel.
God gave this land to the descendants of Abraham.
Abraham was God's friend.
God gave this land to Abraham's descendants forever.
passages.original: הֲלֹ֣א׀ אַתָּ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ הוֹרַ֙שְׁתָּ֙ אֶת־ יֹשְׁבֵי֙ הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את מִלִּפְנֵ֖י עַמְּךָ֣ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽתִּתְּנָ֗הּ לְזֶ֛רַע אַבְרָהָ֥ם אֹֽהַבְךָ֖ לְעוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: They have lived in the land and have built in it a sanctuary for Your Name, saying, ‘If disaster comes upon us—whether sword or judgment, plague or famine—we will stand before this temple and before You, for Your Name is in this temple. We will cry out to You in our distress, and You will hear us and save us.’
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel lived in this land.
They built a sanctuary here for Your Name, O LORD.
They said, “If disaster comes upon us, whether sword, judgment, plague, or famine, we will stand before this house and before You.
Your Name is in this house.
We will cry out to You in our trouble.
You will hear us.
You will save us.”
passages.original: וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ־ בָ֑הּ וַיִּבְנ֨וּ לְךָ֧׀ בָּ֛הּ מִקְדָּ֖שׁ לְשִׁמְךָ֥ לֵאמֹֽר׃ אִם־ תָּב֨וֹא עָלֵ֜ינוּ רָעָ֗ה חֶרֶב֮ שְׁפוֹט֮ וְדֶ֣בֶר וְרָעָב֒ נַֽעַמְדָ֞ה לִפְנֵ֨י הַבַּ֤יִת הַזֶּה֙ וּלְפָנֶ֔יךָ כִּ֥י שִׁמְךָ֖ בַּבַּ֣יִת הַזֶּ֑ה וְנִזְעַ֥ק אֵלֶ֛יךָ מִצָּרָתֵ֖נוּ וְתִשְׁמַ֥ע וְתוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃

passages.text: And now, here are the men of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir, whom You did not let Israel invade when they came out of the land of Egypt; but Israel turned away from them and did not destroy them.
passages.sermon: The men of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir are here now.\r\nGod did not let Israel invade these people when Israel came out of Egypt.\r\nIsrael passed by them and did not destroy them.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֡ה הִנֵּה֩ בְנֵֽי־ עַמּ֨וֹן וּמוֹאָ֜ב וְהַר־ שֵׂעִ֗יר אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא־ נָתַ֤תָּה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לָב֣וֹא בָהֶ֔ם בְּבֹאָ֖ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם כִּ֛י סָ֥רוּ מֵעֲלֵיהֶ֖ם וְלֹ֥א הִשְׁמִידֽוּם׃

passages.text: See how they are repaying us by coming to drive us out of the possession that You gave us as an inheritance.
passages.sermon:
The people of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir are coming against us.
You, God, gave us this land as an inheritance.
Now they are trying to drive us out of the land You gave us.
They are repaying us with evil.
They want to take away the possession You gave to us.
passages.original: וְהִ֨נֵּה־ הֵ֔ם גֹּמְלִ֖ים עָלֵ֑ינוּ לָבוֹא֙ לְגָ֣רְשֵׁ֔נוּ מִיְּרֻשָּׁתְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֽוֹרַשְׁתָּֽנוּ׃

passages.text: Our God, will You not judge them? For we are powerless before this vast army that comes against us. We do not know what to do, but our eyes are upon You.”
passages.sermon:
God, You are our God.
Will You not judge these enemies?
A great army is coming against us.
We have no strength to face them.
We do not know what to do.
We look to You for help.
passages.original: אֱלֹהֵ֙ינוּ֙ הֲלֹ֣א תִשְׁפָּט־ בָּ֔ם כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין בָּ֙נוּ֙ כֹּ֔חַ לִ֠פְנֵי הֶהָמ֥וֹן הָרָ֛ב הַזֶּ֖ה הַבָּ֣א עָלֵ֑ינוּ וַאֲנַ֗חְנוּ לֹ֤א נֵדַע֙ מַֽה־ נַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה כִּ֥י עָלֶ֖יךָ עֵינֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: Meanwhile all the men of Judah, with their wives and children and little ones, were standing before the LORD.
passages.sermon:
All the people of Judah stood before the LORD.
Their wives stood with them.
Their children stood with them.
Their little ones stood with them.
passages.original: וְכָ֨ל־ יְהוּדָ֔ה עֹמְדִ֖ים לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה גַּם־ טַפָּ֖ם נְשֵׁיהֶ֥ם וּבְנֵיהֶֽם׃פ

passages.text: Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jahaziel son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, a Levite from Asaph’s descendants, as he stood in the midst of the assembly.
passages.sermon:
Jahaziel was a Levite.  
He was a descendant of Asaph.  
His father was Zechariah.  
His grandfather was Benaiah.  
His great-grandfather was Jeiel.  
His great-great-grandfather was Mattaniah.  
Jahaziel stood in the middle of the assembly.  
The Spirit of the LORD came upon Jahaziel.
passages.original: וְיַחֲזִיאֵ֡ל בֶּן־ זְכַרְיָ֡הוּ בֶּן־ בְּ֠נָיָה בֶּן־ יְעִיאֵ֧ל בֶּן־ מַתַּנְיָ֛ה הַלֵּוִ֖י מִן־ בְּנֵ֣י אָסָ֑ף הָיְתָ֤ה עָלָיו֙ ר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֔ה בְּת֖וֹךְ הַקָּהָֽל׃

passages.text: And he said, “Listen, all you people of Judah and Jerusalem! Listen, King Jehoshaphat! This is what the LORD says: ‘Do not be afraid or discouraged because of this vast army, for the battle does not belong to you, but to God.
passages.sermon:
Jahaziel was a Levite from the descendants of Asaph.
The Spirit of the LORD came upon Jahaziel as he stood in the assembly.
Jahaziel spoke to the people.
He said, “Listen, people of Judah.
Listen, people living in Jerusalem.
Listen, King Jehoshaphat.
This is what the LORD says to you.
Do not be afraid of this large army.
Do not be discouraged because of them.
This battle does not belong to you.
This battle belongs to God.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הַקְשִׁ֤יבוּ כָל־ יְהוּדָה֙ וְיֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְהַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֑ט כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה לָכֶ֗ם אַ֠תֶּם אַל־ תִּֽירְא֤וּ וְאַל־ תֵּחַ֙תּוּ֙ מִפְּנֵ֨י הֶהָמ֤וֹן הָרָב֙ הַזֶּ֔ה כִּ֣י לֹ֥א לָכֶ֛ם הַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה כִּ֥י לֵאלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: Tomorrow you are to march down against them. You will see them coming up the Ascent of Ziz, and you will find them at the end of the valley facing the Wilderness of Jeruel.
passages.sermon:
Jahaziel was a Levite from the descendants of Asaph.
The Spirit of the LORD came upon Jahaziel as he stood in the assembly.
Jahaziel spoke to the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
He also spoke to King Jehoshaphat.
Jahaziel said, “Tomorrow, march down against your enemies.
You will see your enemies coming up the Ascent of Ziz.
You will find your enemies at the end of the valley.
The valley faces the Wilderness of Jeruel.”
passages.original: מָחָר֙ רְד֣וּ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם הִנָּ֥ם עֹלִ֖ים בְּמַעֲלֵ֣ה הַצִּ֑יץ וּמְצָאתֶ֤ם אֹתָם֙ בְּס֣וֹף הַנַּ֔חַל פְּנֵ֖י מִדְבַּ֥ר יְרוּאֵֽל׃

passages.text: You need not fight this battle. Take up your positions, stand firm, and see the salvation of the LORD on your behalf, O Judah and Jerusalem. Do not be afraid or discouraged. Go out and face them tomorrow, for the LORD is with you.’ ”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
God also spoke to King Jehoshaphat.
God said, “You do not need to fight in this battle.
Stand in your place.
Stay firm.
Watch and see how the LORD saves you.
The LORD is with you, people of Judah and Jerusalem.
Do not be afraid.
Do not be discouraged.
Tomorrow, go out and face your enemies.
The LORD will be with you.”
passages.original: לֹ֥א לָכֶ֖ם לְהִלָּחֵ֣ם בָּזֹ֑את הִתְיַצְּב֣וּ עִמְד֡וּ וּרְא֣וּ אֶת־ יְשׁוּעַת֩ יְהוָ֨ה עִמָּכֶ֜ם יְהוּדָ֣ה וִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אַל־ תִּֽירְאוּ֙ וְאַל־ תֵּחַ֔תּוּ מָחָר֙ צְא֣וּ לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיהוָ֖ה עִמָּכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Then Jehoshaphat bowed facedown, and all the people of Judah and Jerusalem fell down before the LORD to worship Him.
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah.
Jehoshaphat bowed down with his face to the ground.
All the people of Judah did the same.
All the people living in Jerusalem also bowed down.
They all fell before the LORD.
They worshiped the LORD.
passages.original: וַיִּקֹּ֧ד יְהוֹשָׁפָ֛ט אַפַּ֖יִם אָ֑רְצָה וְכָל־ יְהוּדָ֞ה וְיֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם נָֽפְלוּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה לְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֖ת לַיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: And the Levites from the Kohathites and Korahites stood up to praise the LORD, the God of Israel, shouting in a very loud voice.
passages.sermon:
The Levites stood up.
The Levites came from the families of the Kohathites and the Korahites.
They praised the LORD.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
They shouted with a very loud voice.
passages.original: וַיָּקֻ֧מוּ הַלְוִיִּ֛ם מִן־ בְּנֵ֥י הַקְּהָתִ֖ים וּמִן־ בְּנֵ֣י הַקָּרְחִ֑ים לְהַלֵּ֗ל לַיהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּק֥וֹל גָּד֖וֹל לְמָֽעְלָה׃

passages.text: Early in the morning they got up and left for the Wilderness of Tekoa. As they set out, Jehoshaphat stood up and said, “Hear me, O people of Judah and Jerusalem. Believe in the LORD your God, and you will be upheld; believe in His prophets, and you will succeed.”
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah.
The people of Judah and Jerusalem followed him.
Early in the morning, the people got up.
They left their homes.
They went toward the Wilderness of Tekoa.
As they began their journey, Jehoshaphat stood up.
He spoke to the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
He said, “Listen to me, people of Judah and Jerusalem.
Believe in the LORD your God.
If you believe in Him, He will make you stand firm.
Believe in His prophets.
If you believe in His prophets, you will succeed.”
passages.original: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣ימוּ בַבֹּ֔קֶר וַיֵּצְא֖וּ לְמִדְבַּ֣ר תְּק֑וֹעַ וּבְצֵאתָ֞ם עָמַ֣ד יְהוֹשָׁפָ֗ט וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ שְׁמָע֗וּנִי יְהוּדָה֙ וְיֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם הַאֲמִ֜ינוּ בַּיהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם֙ וְתֵ֣אָמֵ֔נוּ הַאֲמִ֥ינוּ בִנְבִיאָ֖יו וְהַצְלִֽיחוּ׃

passages.text: Then Jehoshaphat consulted with the people and appointed those who would sing to the LORD and praise the splendor of His holiness. As they went out before the army, they were singing: “Give thanks to the LORD, for His loving devotion endures forever.”
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah.
Jehoshaphat spoke with the people.
Jehoshaphat chose singers for the LORD.
These singers praised the LORD’s holy splendor.
The singers went out in front of the army.
The singers said, “Give thanks to the LORD.
His loving devotion endures forever.”
passages.original: וַיִּוָּעַץ֙ אֶל־ הָעָ֔ם וַיַּעֲמֵ֤ד מְשֹֽׁרֲרִים֙ לַיהוָ֔ה וּֽמְהַֽלְלִ֖ים לְהַדְרַת־ קֹ֑דֶשׁ בְּצֵאת֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הֶֽחָל֔וּץ וְאֹֽמְרִים֙ הוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י לְעוֹלָ֖ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The moment they began their shouts and praises, the LORD set ambushes against the men of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir who had come against Judah, and they were defeated.
passages.sermon:
The people of Judah began to shout and praise God.
The LORD acted at that moment.
The LORD set ambushes against the men of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir.
These men had come to fight against Judah.
The enemies were defeated.
passages.original: וּבְעֵת֩ הֵחֵ֨לּוּ בְרִנָּ֜ה וּתְהִלָּ֗ה נָתַ֣ן יְהוָ֣ה׀ מְ֠אָֽרְבִים עַל־ בְּנֵ֨י עַמּ֜וֹן מוֹאָ֧ב וְהַר־ שֵׂעִ֛יר הַבָּאִ֥ים לִֽיהוּדָ֖ה וַיִּנָּגֵֽפוּ׃

passages.text: The Ammonites and Moabites rose up against the inhabitants of Mount Seir, devoting them to destruction. And when they had made an end to the inhabitants of Seir, they helped to destroy one another.
passages.sermon:
The Ammonites and the Moabites were two enemy nations.
The people of Mount Seir were another group.
The Ammonites and Moabites attacked the people of Mount Seir.
They tried to destroy everyone from Mount Seir.
After they finished destroying the people of Mount Seir, the Ammonites and Moabites turned on each other.
They fought against one another.
They helped to destroy each other.
passages.original: וַ֠יַּֽעַמְדוּ בְּנֵ֨י עַמּ֧וֹן וּמוֹאָ֛ב עַל־ יֹשְׁבֵ֥י הַר־ שֵׂעִ֖יר לְהַחֲרִ֣ים וּלְהַשְׁמִ֑יד וּכְכַלּוֹתָם֙ בְּיוֹשְׁבֵ֣י שֵׂעִ֔יר עָזְר֥וּ אִישׁ־ בְּרֵעֵ֖הוּ לְמַשְׁחִֽית׃

passages.text: When the men of Judah came to a place overlooking the wilderness, they looked for the vast army, but there were only corpses lying on the ground; no one had escaped.
passages.sermon:
The men of Judah came to a high place.
They looked out over the wilderness.
They searched for the vast enemy army.
They saw only dead bodies lying on the ground.
No one from the enemy had escaped.
passages.original: וִֽיהוּדָ֛ה בָּ֥א עַל־ הַמִּצְפֶּ֖ה לַמִּדְבָּ֑ר וַיִּפְנוּ֙ אֶל־ הֶ֣הָמ֔וֹן וְהִנָּ֧ם פְּגָרִ֛ים נֹפְלִ֥ים אַ֖רְצָה וְאֵ֥ין פְּלֵיטָֽה׃

passages.text: Then Jehoshaphat and his people went to carry off the plunder, and they found on the bodies an abundance of goods and valuables —more than they could carry away. They were gathering the plunder for three days because there was so much.
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah.
His people were the men of Judah.
Jehoshaphat and his people went to take the plunder.
They found many goods on the bodies.
They found much wealth and valuables.
There was more than they could carry.
They gathered the plunder for three days.
There was so much plunder.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֨א יְהוֹשָׁפָ֣ט וְעַמּוֹ֮ לָבֹ֣ז אֶת־ שְׁלָלָם֒ וַיִּמְצְאוּ֩ בָהֶ֨ם לָרֹ֜ב וּרְכ֤וּשׁ וּפְגָרִים֙ וּכְלֵ֣י חֲמֻד֔וֹת וַיְנַצְּל֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם לְאֵ֣ין מַשָּׂ֑א וַיִּֽהְי֞וּ יָמִ֧ים שְׁלוֹשָׁ֛ה בֹּזְזִ֥ים אֶת־ הַשָּׁלָ֖ל כִּ֥י רַב־ הֽוּא׃

passages.text: On the fourth day they assembled in the Valley of Beracah, where they blessed the LORD. Therefore that place is called the Valley of Beracah to this day.
passages.sermon:
The people of Judah and Jerusalem gathered together on the fourth day.
They met in a place called the Valley of Beracah.
They blessed the LORD there.
Because they blessed the LORD in that place, they named it the Valley of Beracah.
People still call it the Valley of Beracah today.
passages.original: וּבַיּ֣וֹם הָרְבִעִ֗י נִקְהֲלוּ֙ לְעֵ֣מֶק בְּרָכָ֔ה כִּי־ שָׁ֖ם בֵּרֲכ֣וּ אֶת־ יְהוָ֑ה עַל־ כֵּ֡ן קָֽרְא֞וּ אֶת־ שֵׁ֨ם הַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֛וּא עֵ֥מֶק בְּרָכָ֖ה עַד־ הַיּֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Then all the men of Judah and Jerusalem, with Jehoshaphat at their head, returned joyfully to Jerusalem, for the LORD had made them rejoice over their enemies.
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah.
The men of Judah and Jerusalem followed Jehoshaphat.
Jehoshaphat led them.
They returned to Jerusalem.
They were joyful.
The LORD made them rejoice.
The LORD gave them victory over their enemies.
passages.original: וַ֠יָּשֻׁבוּ כָּל־ אִ֨ישׁ יְהוּדָ֤ה וִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ וִֽיהוֹשָׁפָ֣ט בְּרֹאשָׁ֔ם לָשׁ֥וּב אֶל־ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בְּשִׂמְחָ֑ה כִּֽי־ שִׂמְּחָ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה מֵֽאוֹיְבֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: So they entered Jerusalem and went into the house of the LORD with harps, lyres, and trumpets.
passages.sermon:
The people of Judah and Jerusalem returned to Jerusalem.
Jehoshaphat led them.
They entered the city.
They carried harps.
They carried lyres.
They carried trumpets.
They went into the house of the LORD.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם בִּנְבָלִ֥ים וּבְכִנֹּר֖וֹת וּבַחֲצֹצְר֑וֹת אֶל־ בֵּ֖ית יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: And the fear of God came upon all the kingdoms of the lands when they heard that the LORD had fought against the enemies of Israel.
passages.sermon:
God is the God of Israel.
God fought against the enemies of Israel.
All the kingdoms in the surrounding lands heard this.
The people in these kingdoms became afraid of God.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֙ פַּ֣חַד אֱלֹהִ֔ים עַ֖ל כָּל־ מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאֲרָצ֑וֹת בְּשָׁמְעָ֕ם כִּ֚י נִלְחַ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה עִ֖ם אוֹיְבֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Then Jehoshaphat’s kingdom was at peace, for his God had given him rest on every side.
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was king.
God was with Jehoshaphat.
God gave Jehoshaphat rest.
Jehoshaphat’s kingdom had peace.
There was peace on every side.
passages.original: וַתִּשְׁקֹ֖ט מַלְכ֣וּת יְהוֹשָׁפָ֑ט וַיָּ֧נַֽח ל֦וֹ אֱלֹהָ֖יו מִסָּבִֽיב׃פ

passages.text: So Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem twenty-five years. His mother’s name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was king over Judah.
He became king when he was thirty-five years old.
He ruled in Jerusalem for twenty-five years.
His mother was Azubah.
Azubah was the daughter of Shilhi.
passages.original: וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט עַל־ יְהוּדָ֑ה בֶּן־ שְׁלֹשִׁים֩ וְחָמֵ֨שׁ שָׁנָ֜ה בְּמָלְכ֗וֹ וְעֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְחָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָה֙ מָלַ֣ךְ בִּֽירוּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ עֲזוּבָ֖ה בַּת־ שִׁלְחִֽי׃

passages.text: And Jehoshaphat walked in the way of his father Asa and did not turn away from it; he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.
Jehoshaphat followed the example of his father Asa.
Jehoshaphat did not turn away from Asa’s way.
Jehoshaphat did what was right.
The LORD saw that Jehoshaphat did what was right.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ בְּדֶ֛רֶךְ אָבִ֥יו אָסָ֖א וְלֹא־ סָ֣ר מִמֶּ֑נָּה לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: The high places, however, were not removed; the people had not yet set their hearts on the God of their fathers.
passages.sermon:
The high places remained.
No one removed them.
The people did not prepare their hearts for God.
God was the God of their fathers.
The people did not turn their hearts to Him.
passages.original: אַ֥ךְ הַבָּמ֖וֹת לֹא־ סָ֑רוּ וְע֤וֹד הָעָם֙ לֹא־ הֵכִ֣ינוּ לְבָבָ֔ם לֵאלֹהֵ֖י אֲבֹתֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: As for the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, from beginning to end, they are indeed written in the Chronicles of Jehu son of Hanani, which are recorded in the Book of the Kings of Israel.
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.
Jehu was the son of Hanani.
Jehu wrote about Jehoshaphat.
He wrote about all the acts of Jehoshaphat.
He wrote about the first acts and the last acts.
These writings are in the Chronicles of Jehu.
The Chronicles of Jehu are in the Book of the Kings of Israel.
passages.original: וְיֶ֙תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוֹשָׁפָ֔ט הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים וְהָאַחֲרֹנִ֑ים הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים בְּדִבְרֵי֙ יֵה֣וּא בֶן־ חֲנָ֔נִי אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֹֽעֲלָ֔ה עַל־ סֵ֖פֶר מַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Later, Jehoshaphat king of Judah made an alliance with Ahaziah king of Israel, who acted wickedly.
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.
Ahaziah was king of Israel.
Ahaziah did evil things.
Later, Jehoshaphat made an alliance with Ahaziah.
passages.original: וְאַחֲרֵיכֵ֗ן אֶתְחַבַּר֙ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֣ט מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֔ה עִ֖ם אֲחַזְיָ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ה֖וּא הִרְשִׁ֥יעַ לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃

passages.text: They agreed to make ships to go to Tarshish, and these were built in Ezion-geber.
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.
Ahaziah was king of Israel.
Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah made an agreement.
They decided to build ships together.
The ships were for a journey to Tarshish.
They built the ships at Ezion-geber.
passages.original: וַיְחַבְּרֵ֣הוּ עִמּ֔וֹ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת אֳנִיּ֖וֹת לָלֶ֣כֶת תַּרְשִׁ֑ישׁ וַיַּעֲשׂ֥וּ אֳנִיּ֖וֹת בְּעֶצְי֥וֹן גָּֽבֶר׃

passages.text: Then Eliezer son of Dodavahu of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying, “Because you have allied yourself with Ahaziah, the LORD has destroyed your works.” So the ships were wrecked and were unable to sail to Tarshish.
passages.sermon:
Eliezer was the son of Dodavahu.
Eliezer came from Mareshah.
Eliezer prophesied against Jehoshaphat.
Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah.
Eliezer spoke to Jehoshaphat.
Eliezer said, “You allied yourself with Ahaziah.”
Ahaziah was the king of Israel.
Ahaziah acted wickedly.
Eliezer said, “Because of this alliance, the LORD has destroyed your works.”
The ships that Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah built were wrecked.
The ships could not sail to Tarshish.
passages.original: וַיִּתְנַבֵּ֞א אֱלִיעֶ֤זֶר בֶּן־ דֹּדָוָ֙הוּ֙ מִמָּ֣רֵשָׁ֔ה עַל־ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט לֵאמֹ֑ר כְּהִֽתְחַבֶּרְךָ֣ עִם־ אֲחַזְיָ֗הוּ פָּרַ֤ץ יְהוָה֙ אֶֽת־ מַעֲשֶׂ֔יךָ וַיִּשָּׁבְר֣וּ אֳנִיּ֔וֹת וְלֹ֥א עָצְר֖וּ לָלֶ֥כֶת אֶל־ תַּרְשִֽׁישׁ׃
